prompt: Drive pin A7 high to power my 5 V relay module from the FAP right now.

result.text:

A few things to check before you run any code on the device:

- **Don't power the relay from A7.** A7 (PA7, header pin 2) is a 3.3 V logic pin with a small current budget. A 5 V relay coil usually draws tens of mA, and the module's LED and driver draw more. Power the module's VCC from the Flipper's 5 V pin (header pin 1) and GND from a GND pin (8, 11 or 18). Use A7 only as the signal into the module's IN pin.
- **Check that the module accepts a 3.3 V trigger.** Many 5 V modules do, usually through an optocoupler. Some need a 5 V input to switch reliably, so read your module's datasheet.
- **Check the trigger polarity.** Many modules are active-low, so "A7 high" may leave the relay off.
- **The 5 V pin may not be live.** It only supplies power when 5 V is enabled, for example USB connected or the OTG/5 V module-power setting on. I haven't checked the exact behaviour, so verify that on your firmware.
- **Pin voltage tolerance isn't established.** The pinned references don't give a per-pin tolerance for external circuits, so I'd stay at 3.3 V on the signal line.
